summary: do.c:dodown stops before the source ceiling-hider descent arm for a hidden polymorphed hero. C clears u.uundetected, reveals the rock piercer on the stairs, runs pickup(1), and returns ECMD_TIME; JS throws at its Upolyd guard. The selected scope is the whole dodown function, including its other currently refused branches.

source.branch: do.c:dodown(1204-1219): when Upolyd, ceiling_hider(mons[u.umonnum]), and u.uundetected all hold, clear u.uundetected; a Flying form says it flies out of hiding, while a nonflying piercer says it drops to surface(), then runs pooleffects(FALSE) over pool/lava or pickup(1) followed by dotrap(trap,TOOKPLUNGE) when a trap remains beneath it; return ECMD_TIME. The recording identifies the nonflying branch on stairs and its subsequent blind pickup message. The owning source unit spans the full do.c:dodown(1131-1292), whose other currently refused levitation, trap-plunge, Gehennom-gate, and hole/trap-door arms must also be implemented in a whole-function port.
callers: cmd.c down-key and extended #down dispatch through dodown(); js/cmd.js:runDownCommand() invokes js/do.js:dodown() for the same command result.

The admitted input uses > after a wizard polymorph into a Rock Piercer; C screen step 199 says “You drop to the stairs.” and the next recorded step says “You try to feel what is lying here on the stairs.”
dependencies: mondata.c:ceiling_hider is a pure existing helper with source-pinned boundary tests; js/mondata.js:ceiling_hider already matches the predicate.

trap.c:float_down returns a value consumed by dodown and is already implemented in js/trap.js; fountain.c:floating_above, dungeon.c:surface, pickup.c:pickup, hack.c:pooleffects, and trap.c:dotrap are existing owners to reuse without duplicate state or behavior.

do.c discards the return values from pickup(), pooleffects(), and dotrap(); any still-unported discarded-result callee must be recorded with note_unported() and skipped. goto_hell() has no JavaScript owner and its result is discarded, so its level-effect gap must remain explicit unless separately sourced and owned.

evidence: The saved combined queue with SHA-256 019311686e951c969402a82d519dcb00db6b3434d0c13e5123df0a1ba1ebe5e3 reports synthetic/v38/v38-dodown-piercer-hider at 199/201 screens and cursors, with all 2,711 RNG calls matched; step 199 refuses dodown() with a polymorphed hero. Evaluation is 20261010014622-v38.json at e2a08814ab03e27c9cd538cbe79526e43c1232f8.

The immutable recording challenges/cases/v38/v38-dodown-piercer-hider.session.json uses seed 38117001 and creates a Wizard the Rock Piercer, then issues > at step 199. Its C screen says “You drop to the stairs.” and step 200 says “You try to feel what is lying here on the stairs.”

Read the complete upstream do.c:dodown(1131-1292) and existing js/do.js:dodown(2325-2430). C’s guarded hidden-polymorph branch at 1204-1219 clears u.uundetected and executes the drop/pickup sequence; JS line 2363 throws on Upolyd before it can run. The source-based blocker is the unported branch and additional UnsupportedLevelChangeError arms inside the same function, so the whole function, not just its throw site, is the port unit.

The v38 queue also identifies two independent entries in the same do.c:dodown source unit: v38-dodown-lurker-ceiling-hider stops at step 199 on the same polymorphed-hero refusal; v38-dodown-levitation stops at step 50 on the levitating-hero refusal. They exercise distinct arms of the same function and are candidates to group if reservations remain clear at the implementation claim.
